Sell an Established Business in India

Selling an established business in India starts with defining the ownership outcome, preparing credible financial information and identifying suitable buyers before sharing sensitive details. Legacy Search helps owners explore succession, majority sales and full exits through a confidential advisory process.

Start a private enquiry ↗

Choose the ownership outcome

A full exit, a controlling-stake sale and a staged succession solve different problems. Decide how much capital you want to realise, whether you want to retain equity or an operating role, and what continuity means for employees and customers. These preferences should shape the buyer shortlist before price negotiations begin.

Prepare a buyer-ready business

Organise three years of financial statements, management accounts, debt and working-capital information, customer concentration, ownership records and material contracts. Separate recurring operating earnings from one-off items. Avoid distributing detailed records until appropriate confidentiality arrangements are in place.

Evaluate a buyer beyond price

Assess financing certainty, strategic rationale, decision-making authority, proposed control rights and transition expectations. An attractive headline valuation is not equivalent to cash at closing: deferred payments, conditions and adjustments may materially change the outcome.

How Legacy Search can help

We begin with the owner’s objectives and business profile, then explore suitable counterparties and coordinate the transaction process alongside the parties’ professional advisers. An initial conversation does not commit you to a sale. Our published mandate value range is ₹100–2,000 crore.

Common questions

Can I explore selling without announcing it publicly?

Yes. Start with a confidential discussion and share identifying information only through an agreed process.

Do I need a final valuation first?

No. A preliminary assessment can guide the search; a defensible valuation requires financial review and market evidence.

General information only; not legal, tax or investment advice. Transaction availability, suitability and execution depend on the circumstances.
